style: An oil painting in the manner of 1890s academic realism: rich dark palette, dramatic chiaroscuro, visible brushwork, painterly and cinematic, 16:9. Transylvania, May 1893, by night under a waning gibbous moon. The moon, where seen, is a waning gibbous, a little past full, never a crescent. No text, no captions, no signature, no frames, no black bars or borders.

beats.text: A calèche has stopped in the vast gloomy courtyard of a ruined castle; dark archways lead off under great round arches; the young traveller looks up from the carriage at the black frowning walls and broken battlements against the moonlit sky. Wide view, the castle dominating.

The hooded driver, face unseen, has jumped down and holds out a hand like a steel vice to help the young traveller alight beside a great old iron-studded door; luggage at their feet; four horses steaming in the cold.

The young traveller stands alone and uncertain in the moonlit courtyard before a huge closed door studded with iron nails, set in a projecting doorway of massive stone; no bell or knocker; dark window openings above. Wide view, the man small.

The great door stands open; within stands the tall old Count, in black, holding an antique silver lamp whose bare flame throws long quivering shadows; his right hand raised in a courtly gesture of welcome.
On the threshold the Count grasps the young Englishman's hand with a grip of steel, cold as ice; the young man winces; lamplight between them, the dark passage behind.
The Count, carrying the luggage himself, leads the young man up a great winding stone stair; their steps ring on the stone; a lamp throws their shadows up the curving wall.
A well-lit bedroom in an old castle: a table spread for supper, a great log fire flaring in a huge stone hearth, heavy old furniture, tapestries; warm firelight after the cold night.

The Count stands at one side of a great stone fireplace, leaning against the stonework, waving a graceful hand toward a supper table where the young Englishman stands; roast chicken, cheese, a bottle of old Tokay.
The Count, standing by the firelight, reads a sealed letter gravely, then smiles; the broken seal in his long fingers.
By the fire: the young Englishman in a chair smokes a cigar, studying his host; the Count sits opposite, firelight on his hard face and pointed ears, his hands on his knees.
A pack of wolves in the valley far below the castle, heads raised, howling under the moon; dark pine forest and mountains, the castle on its crag above. Wide landscape, no people.
